mentl/af8a918:
STAGE 1a of the finish-line plan, the core-ADT half. The census's largest root:
a bare `List` in a declaration is TName("List", []) — a nominal name that never
unifies with the native TList the consumers build via `[..]` literals and every
list op (push/slice/make_list all bind TList). There is no bridge between them,
by design: SYNTAX §4① has ONE sequence kind, written `[a]`, and the nominal
`List` is the drift. So the declaration erased the element type the consumers
prove, and inference reported the conflict at every destructure.

The fix is [Element] at the declaration, never a TName<->TList unify bridge. A
bridge would clear all ~645 at once and that is the trap: it legitimizes an
illegal shape while leaving the element just as erased, only quieter. The
declaration carries the real element the consumers already prove — most sites
named it in a trailing comment the developer wrote but the compiler could not
read (env_snapshot: List, // [EnvEntry]).

Swept here, each verified against its consumer:
  Ty      TTuple [Ty] · TFun [TParam] · TName [Ty] · TRecord/TRecordOpen
          [(String, Ty)]
  Node    CallExpr/BlockExpr/Make{List,Tuple,String} [Node] · LambdaExpr
          [TParam] · MatchExpr [(Pat, Node)] · ResumeExpr [{init, name}] ·
          Make/Update/NamedRecord [(String, Node)]
  Pat     PCon/PTuple/PList/PAlt [Pat] · PRecord [(String, Pat)]
  LowExpr/LowPat/LowFn   the projected-read siblings LSuspend already typed
  Scheme/SchemeKind/EffRow/EffName/Graph/Env/CursorView + the lower/infer
          effect-op signatures, all read live from where the value flows

The same sweep cleared `N vs Node` (14 -> 0): several record shapes wrote
`body: N` / `init: N` — the constructor name of `type Node = N(...)` — where the
type Node was meant, so it read as nominal TName("N",[]). The handler-arm and
state-field records (types/parser/lower/infer) are made consistent as one shape.

Two substrate-aligned fixes mirroring the seed's task #115 + #109 patterns
at the wheel layer. Both use canonical projection (per-handle locals +
list_index iteration) — no shared scratches, no LIFO surprises.

1. emit_lcall + emit_ltailcall use $call_<h> per-handle scratch
   instead of shared $state_tmp (wasm.mn:1217-1245).

   Mirrors bootstrap/src/emit/emit_call.wat's emit_lcall (task #115).
   The wheel's emit was never updated to match the seed; this completes
   the substrate alignment. Each call site's closure-as-state is named
   by the call's graph handle — canonical projection.

2. emit_expr_list iterates FIFO via list_index instead of
   list_head/list_tail (wasm.mn:1706-1714).

   Mirrors emit_body's f030db5 fix. The runtime list convention is
   snoc-stack (list_head returns SEMANTIC-LAST per
   lib/runtime/lists.mn:9), so list_head/list_tail iteration walks
   args in REVERSE — corrupting calls with multi-arg lists. FIFO
   list_index iteration matches semantic order regardless of storage.

3. emit_let_locals_expr's LCall/LTailCall arms declare $call_<h>
   in the fn preamble (wasm.mn:1026-1037).

   Per WAT discipline: locals must be declared at fn scope before
   use. The walk that discovers fn-level locals now also discovers
   per-call-handle scratches.
